name: Caesar cut

lead: The Caesar cut is a short haircut with hair layered to roughly 2 to 5 cm all over and short bangs cut straight across the forehead. It is a simple, structured style that has been popular among Western men since the 1980s.
For looks, the forward fringe gives a defined horizontal line over the brow and, according to Grokipedia, can make a receding hairline or thin crown less noticeable.

paras: A barber cuts the top to an even short length with a blunt fringe and usually tapers or fades the sides. Daily styling is described as a small amount of pomade or matte clay worked forward, with washing a few times a week.
No health risks are documented. The look depends on hair density and hairline shape, and sources describe it as suiting some face shapes, notably oval and square, more than others.

lead: The Caesar cut is a hairstyle with short bangs cut straight across and hair layered to about 2 to 5 cm all over [1]. Wikipedia says it is named after the Roman emperor Augustus, whose portraits often show a similar cut, and that it became fashionable among Western boys and men in the 1980s [1].

Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, instead ties the name to Julius Caesar, who it says combed hair forward to hide a receding hairline, citing the Roman historian Suetonius [2]. Sources therefore differ on which Roman the name refers to.

As a looksmaxxing-adjacent style, the Caesar cut is valued as a low-effort way to frame the face and to disguise a receding hairline or thin crown [2]. Celebrities named as wearers include George Clooney, David Beckham and Tom Holland [2], and Wikipedia mentions Mark Zuckerberg wearing it in the past [1].

paras: Grokipedia describes a blunt fringe at eyebrow level, layered top and tapered or faded sides and back, produced with clippers and shears [2]. It says the style suits oval and square faces and is used by men with receding hairlines [2].

Wikipedia attributes the name to Augustus [1]. Grokipedia attributes it to Julius Caesar and notes the modern cut is a homage rather than a replica of an ancient style [2]. Because Grokipedia is AI-generated, it should be read with care.
Grokipedia describes a small amount of pomade or matte clay applied to slightly damp hair and brushed forward, and washing two to three times a week [2].

timeline.event: The cut becomes fashionable among Western boys and men [1].
Grokipedia says George Clooney's role on ER from 1994 helped popularise the cut [2].
